nodes.text: Welcome to the hall! Mind the sawdust — actually no, don't mind it, sawdust on the floor means work on the bench. I'm *Tilo*. Loom, carving bench, and worktable, all public. The town that makes things together mends together.
What can I do for you?

choices.text: Public? Anyone can use these stations?
Your sister says you never finish anything.
You trained somewhere grand, I'd guess.

nodes.text: Anyone with the patience. That's the whole idea — a croft can't afford a loom, but a *town* can afford one everybody shares. Bring hide, cloth, or timber; leave with something that didn't exist at breakfast. Finest feeling there is.

Merra told you about the chair. Of course she did. Three years, yes. But understand: the chair is *teaching* me. Every joint I cut for pay, I cut better because the chair at home is watching. She sells eggs; she wouldn't understand a long apprenticeship to your own furniture.

Silverfall's galleria — a clothier took me on as a boy to carry bolts up the Silver Stair. I came down before the deep trouble with one pattern-book and a needle case. The mountain teaches you the *grand* way to do things. The ford taught me the useful way. Between the two you get a decent craftsman.
Leather, cloth, and woodcraft patterns — the whole soft-trades ladder. Priced by what they'll ask of your hands.
